summary: IDS s106_single is degraded: 7.9% of frames (226/2859, up to 8058 bytes) exceed the tool's 1518-byte MTU and are dropped by its NIC, creating blind spot. No other visibility faults detected.

findings.root_cause: Upstream network/broker is forwarding jumbo frames (observed up to 8058 bytes) to a 1 Gbps IDS port limited to 1518 bytes. The packet broker is not normalizing MTU/slicing, so the IDS NIC drops oversize frames at ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops ~7.9% of frames before inspection. As IDS needs_full_payload=true and needs_both_directions, any attack, exploit or C2 payload carried in those large frames is completely missed, reducing detection coverage and breaking flow reassembly for those sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Tool requires full payload so broker slicing to 1518 would truncate payload and break IDS signatures. Instead enable 9000-byte jumbo support on IDS NIC/tool or configure packet broker to normalize MTU (fragment/slice with header preservation only if jumbo cannot be enabled) so frames are delivered without NIC drops while preserving payload for inspection.
